work.title: The Life and Death of King Richard the Second
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 1, Scene 4
scene.title: SCENE IV. London. A Room in the King's Castle
scene.location: London. A Room in the King's Castle

content.text: Enter King Richard, Green and Bagot at one door; Aumerle at another.

lines.text: We did observe.—Cousin Aumerle,
lines.plainText: We did observeCousin Aumerle

lines.text: How far brought you high Hereford on his way?
lines.plainText: How far brought you high Hereford on his way

lines.text: I brought high Hereford, if you call him so,
lines.plainText: I brought high Hereford if you call him so

lines.text: But to the next highway, and there I left him.
lines.plainText: But to the next highway and there I left him

lines.text: And say, what store of parting tears were shed?
lines.plainText: And say what store of parting tears were shed

lines.text: Faith, none for me, except the northeast wind,
lines.plainText: Faith none for me except the northeast wind

lines.text: Which then blew bitterly against our faces,
lines.plainText: Which then blew bitterly against our faces

lines.text: Awaked the sleeping rheum, and so by chance
lines.plainText: Awaked the sleeping rheum and so by chance

lines.text: Did grace our hollow parting with a tear.
lines.plainText: Did grace our hollow parting with a tear

lines.text: What said our cousin when you parted with him?
lines.plainText: What said our cousin when you parted with him

lines.text: "Farewell."
lines.plainText: Farewell

lines.text: And, for my heart disdained that my tongue
lines.plainText: And for my heart disdained that my tongue

lines.text: Should so profane the word, that taught me craft
lines.plainText: Should so profane the word that taught me craft

lines.text: To counterfeit oppression of such grief
lines.plainText: To counterfeit oppression of such grief

lines.text: That words seemed buried in my sorrow's grave.
lines.plainText: That words seemed buried in my sorrow's grave

lines.text: Marry, would the word "farewell" have lengthened hours
lines.plainText: Marry would the word farewell have lengthened hours

lines.text: And added years to his short banishment,
lines.plainText: And added years to his short banishment

lines.text: He should have had a volume of farewells,
lines.plainText: He should have had a volume of farewells

lines.text: But since it would not, he had none of me.
lines.plainText: But since it would not he had none of me

lines.text: He is our cousin, cousin, but 'tis doubt,
lines.plainText: He is our cousin cousin but 'tis doubt

lines.text: When time shall call him home from banishment,
lines.plainText: When time shall call him home from banishment

lines.text: Whether our kinsman come to see his friends.
lines.plainText: Whether our kinsman come to see his friends

lines.text: Ourself and Bushy, Bagot here and Green,
lines.plainText: Ourself and Bushy Bagot here and Green

lines.text: Observed his courtship to the common people,
lines.plainText: Observed his courtship to the common people

lines.text: How he did seem to dive into their hearts
lines.plainText: How he did seem to dive into their hearts

lines.text: With humble and familiar courtesy,
lines.plainText: With humble and familiar courtesy

lines.text: What reverence he did throw away on slaves,
lines.plainText: What reverence he did throw away on slaves

lines.text: Wooing poor craftsmen with the craft of smiles
lines.plainText: Wooing poor craftsmen with the craft of smiles

lines.text: And patient underbearing of his fortune,
lines.plainText: And patient underbearing of his fortune

lines.text: As 'twere to banish their affects with him.
lines.plainText: As 'twere to banish their affects with him

lines.text: Off goes his bonnet to an oyster-wench;
lines.plainText: Off goes his bonnet to an oysterwench

lines.text: A brace of draymen bid God speed him well,
lines.plainText: A brace of draymen bid God speed him well

lines.text: And had the tribute of his supple knee,
lines.plainText: And had the tribute of his supple knee

lines.text: With "Thanks, my countrymen, my loving friends",
lines.plainText: With Thanks my countrymen my loving friends

lines.text: As were our England in reversion his,
lines.plainText: As were our England in reversion his

lines.text: And he our subjects' next degree in hope.
lines.plainText: And he our subjects' next degree in hope

lines.text: Well, he is gone, and with him go these thoughts.
lines.plainText: Well he is gone and with him go these thoughts

lines.text: Now for the rebels which stand out in Ireland,
lines.plainText: Now for the rebels which stand out in Ireland

lines.text: Expedient manage must be made, my liege,
lines.plainText: Expedient manage must be made my liege

lines.text: Ere further leisure yield them further means
lines.plainText: Ere further leisure yield them further means

lines.text: For their advantage and your highness' loss.
lines.plainText: For their advantage and your highness' loss

lines.text: We will ourself in person to this war.
lines.plainText: We will ourself in person to this war

lines.text: And, for our coffers, with too great a court
lines.plainText: And for our coffers with too great a court

lines.text: And liberal largess, are grown somewhat light,
lines.plainText: And liberal largess are grown somewhat light

lines.text: We are enforced to farm our royal realm,
lines.plainText: We are enforced to farm our royal realm

lines.text: The revenue whereof shall furnish us
lines.plainText: The revenue whereof shall furnish us

lines.text: For our affairs in hand. If that come short,
lines.plainText: For our affairs in hand If that come short

lines.text: Our substitutes at home shall have blank charters
lines.plainText: Our substitutes at home shall have blank charters

lines.text: Whereto, when they shall know what men are rich,
lines.plainText: Whereto when they shall know what men are rich

lines.text: They shall subscribe them for large sums of gold,
lines.plainText: They shall subscribe them for large sums of gold

lines.text: And send them after to supply our wants;
lines.plainText: And send them after to supply our wants

lines.text: For we will make for Ireland presently.
lines.plainText: For we will make for Ireland presently

lines.text: Old John of Gaunt is grievous sick, my lord,
lines.plainText: Old John of Gaunt is grievous sick my lord

lines.text: Suddenly taken, and hath sent posthaste
lines.plainText: Suddenly taken and hath sent posthaste

lines.text: To entreat your Majesty to visit him.
lines.plainText: To entreat your Majesty to visit him

lines.text: Where lies he?
lines.plainText: Where lies he

lines.text: At Ely House.
lines.plainText: At Ely House

lines.text: Now put it, God, in his physician's mind
lines.plainText: Now put it God in his physician's mind

lines.text: To help him to his grave immediately!
lines.plainText: To help him to his grave immediately

lines.text: The lining of his coffers shall make coats
lines.plainText: The lining of his coffers shall make coats

lines.text: To deck our soldiers for these Irish wars.
lines.plainText: To deck our soldiers for these Irish wars

lines.text: Come, gentlemen, let's all go visit him.
lines.plainText: Come gentlemen let's all go visit him

lines.text: Pray God we may make haste and come too late!
lines.plainText: Pray God we may make haste and come too late

lines.text: Amen!
lines.plainText: Amen
